name: hurst_exponent_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The Hurst exponent (H) measures the long-range dependence of a time series. H > 0.5 indicates persistence (trending), H < 0.5 indicates anti-persistence (mean-reverting), and H = 0.5 indicates a random walk. By computing the rolling Hurst exponent on 1-min returns using the rescaled range (R/S) method over 60 bars, we classify the current regime and select the appropriate strategy. H > 0.55: trend-follow with EMA crossover. H < 0.45: mean-revert with Bollinger Bands. 0.45-0.55: random walk, no edge, stay flat. The inefficiency exists because Hurst exponent computation is mathematically sophisticated, and its application to 1-min intraday trading is virtually absent in publicly available strategies.
mechanism: Market microstructure varies across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes, mean-reversion dominates as market makers provide tight liquidity. In high-vol regimes, momentum persists as liquidity thins and stop-cascades amplify moves. Adapting the signal to the current regime captures the appropriate edge for prevailing conditions.

conditions: PERSISTENT: Hurst_Regime == PERSISTENT AND EMA(close,8) > EMA(close,20) AND close > vwap
ANTI_PERSIST: Hurst_Regime == ANTI_PERSIST AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap
PERSISTENT: Hurst_Regime == PERSISTENT AND EMA(close,8) < EMA(close,20) AND close < vwap
ANTI_PERSIST: Hurst_Regime == ANTI_PERSIST AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap

weaknesses: R/S Hurst exponent on 60 data points is statistically unreliable — the estimator has high variance with small samples, and 60 1-min bars is far below the recommended minimum of 256 for accurate Hurst estimation
Late session start (10:15) due to 60-bar warm-up means missing the morning volatility window where many intraday opportunities occur
The Hurst exponent is a global property of the series within the window — it may not reflect the very recent (last 5-10 bar) dynamics, causing signals that are backward-looking
prior_art: Mandelbrot (1972) on R/S analysis; Peters (1994) 'Fractal Market Analysis'; Di Matteo et al. (2005) on Hurst exponent for financial time series; intraday application is novel but builds on well-established theory
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
